name: Crucible Industries Memory Alloy Switchblade MS-6 'Recall'
description:
A folding knife with a blade constructed from shape-memory alloy that returns to its factory-set geometry after being deformed by impact, bending, or deliberate reshaping. The Recall's blade can be bent 90 degrees, twisted, or even partially flattened, and within seconds it will flow back to its original razor-edged profile. The weapon cannot be permanently damaged by any force short of melting it.

The MS-6's shape-memory blade is activated by body heat — the alloy's transition temperature is set at 32 degrees Celsius, meaning the blade begins self-correcting the moment it is held in a warm hand. When cold, the blade is malleable enough to be bent and hidden in configurations that do not resemble a weapon — folded flat against a belt buckle, coiled inside a bracelet housing, or compressed into a cylinder that looks like a pen. Once warmed by body contact, it unfolds and rigidizes into a fighting knife within four seconds.

Crucible developed the Recall as a concealment weapon for operatives who face thorough physical searches. The blade's ability to be deformed into non-weapon shapes defeats visual inspection and manual pat-downs. Standard weapon scanners detect its metallic signature, but the shape presented to the scanner does not match weapon profiles in detection databases, often resulting in the blade being classified as a harmless personal item.
specifications:
blade_length: 12 cm (deployed)
total_length: 24 cm (deployed), variable when deformed
weight: 140 g
blade_material: Crucible proprietary shape-memory alloy
transition_temperature: 32°C (body heat activation)
recovery_time: 4 seconds from maximum deformation
edge_retention: Self-restoring — infinite edge life
tactical_use: The Recall is a last-resort weapon for operatives who have been disarmed or searched. Its deformation concealment allows it to survive screening that would catch rigid blades, and its body-heat activation means it is always available when held. The self-restoring edge means the blade never needs sharpening — each use returns it to factory precision. In combat, the blade's shape-memory properties make it resistant to techniques that target the weapon (bending the blade out of line, for example, is pointless). The primary limitation is the blade's modest size — it is a close-combat knife, not a fighting sword.
cultural_context: The Recall has become a symbol of persistence in GLMZ's operative culture — a weapon that cannot be broken, only temporarily inconvenienced. The phrase 'memory alloy' has entered slang to describe a person who bounces back from setbacks with their original form intact. The weapon's concealment capability has also made it a favorite among individuals who live in permanent states of potential threat — people who sleep with a Recall hidden in their clothing because they never know when they will need to fight their way out.
story_hooks: A Recall blade was found at a crime scene in a shape that should not be possible — the alloy was deformed into a configuration that exceeds its rated recovery capability, suggesting someone has modified the memory alloy's crystal structure.

A political prisoner was stripped, searched, and held in a bare cell for three days. On the fourth day, they were found with a Recall blade. No one can explain how it got past the search — or who provided it.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek folding knife with an almost organic quality to its design. When deployed, it presents a traditional fighting knife silhouette with a subtly curved blade that catches light along its edge. The handle is compact and ergonomic, designed for concealment as much as combat. In its cold, deformed state, the blade can appear warped or coiled with an unsettling flexibility that betrays its exotic material.
physical_description.dimensions: 12 cm blade length (deployed), 24 cm total length (deployed). When deformed for concealment, blade can compress to 3-5 cm thickness depending on configuration.
physical_description.weight_description: Surprisingly light in hand at 140 grams — balanced toward the blade despite the modest heft. Feels almost delicate when cold, but carries a sense of contained potential.
physical_description.primary_material: Crucible proprietary shape-memory alloy blade; aerospace-grade titanium-reinforced polymer handle with embedded thermal sensors
physical_description.finish: Satin-brushed memory alloy with a faint iridescent sheen that shifts subtly as light plays across the surface. Handle features a matte charcoal composite with brushed metal accents.
physical_description.color_scheme: Silvered gray blade with hints of blue undertone in certain light angles. Charcoal-black handle with gunmetal gray frame components and minimal accent striping in faint copper.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer grip with subtle raised diamond pattern for retention even in gloved hands. Frame components are smooth but deliberately etched to prevent slipping.
distinctive_features: Blade exhibits faint metallic striations visible in certain angles, marking the memory alloy's crystalline structure
Subtle thermal indicator strip embedded in the spine — color shifts from blue (cold/inactive) to red (warmed/active)
Minimalist handle design with no excessive ornamentation — pure function
Blade profile shows an almost liquid quality when deformed, as if caught mid-transformation
Frame lock mechanism is nearly invisible, integrated into the handle spine
Crucible Industries manufacturer mark is laser-etched and nearly flush with the handle surface
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: CRUCIBLE INDUSTRIES mark appears as a subtle geometric logo on the handle spine near the frame lock. Serial number etched microscopically on the blade tang, visible only under magnification. No aggressive branding — designed for operatives who prefer discretion.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn specimens show micro-scratches on the blade face that fade within hours as the alloy self-restores. Handle polymer may show patina from extended use but remains functionally unmarked. The weapon ages gracefully, with no visible degradation even after years of deployment.
